messages:
Jordan: Hey people-ops — my wallet (and insurance ID card) was stolen in Madrid yesterday. I got urgent care at a local clinic and they gave me an itemized invoice in EUR. I need to submit for reimbursement and the pharmacy needs proof-of-coverage to fill a script. What do you need from me?

People Ops: Oh no, sorry that happened. We'll help. Please attach photos of the itemized invoice and proof of payment (card swipe or bank txn). We also need provider name, address, and any tax ID or NPI on the invoice. If the provider doesn’t include a tax ID we can accept a signed provider attestation.

People Ops: For foreign currency claims: submit original receipts in EUR + either a bank statement showing the exact charge in EUR and the converted USD amount OR a screenshot of the FX rate on the date of service and your calculation. Reimbursements are paid in USD using the exchange rate on the date of service.

Claims Team: Quick checklist (you can paste this into the portal upload description):
```
- Itemized invoice (original, photo ok)
- Proof of payment (card txn or bank statement)
- Date of service
- Provider name + address (and tax id / NPI if available)
- Diagnosis/procedure codes if provided
- English translation of invoice if not in English (line-by-line)
- Currency conversion evidence (bank stmt or FX screenshot + calc)
```

Claims Team: If provider lacks a tax id we’ll accept a signed attestation from the clinic confirming identity and services. Attach that as a PDF.

Jordan: Attached invoice_001.jpg and photo_2026.jpg (photos of the receipt). Provider is "Clínica San José" — no tax id on the receipt but it has a clinic stamp and a handwritten provider name. I also have the card transaction screenshot. The invoice is in Spanish and the clinic included a short procedure note but no CPT.

Zoe Patel: FYI Jordan — when I filed from Barcelona last year they asked for a literal English translation of the invoice (just a 1‑page line-by-line). I just did a selfie-photo with annotations and it worked.

People Ops: Good note, Zoe. Jordan, please add a short English translation file (can be a text note). Also tell us if the pharmacy needs the coverage letter emailed or printed at the counter. If you want us to email them, give us the pharmacy email and we’ll cc you.

Jordan: Pharmacy wants an email to release meds — Farmacia Central <farmacia@example.es>. Also quick q: is there a preferred subject line or reference for the claim upload?

Claims Team: Use this subject when uploading and in the email subject so we can route quickly:
```
Reimbursement Request — Jordan Rivera — Foreign Receipts — Claim 1768889999
```
We’ll assign an internal claim ID after we receive the upload.

Benefits Bot: Reminder: please upload via the benefits portal (https://benefits.redwood.com/claims -> "Upload foreign receipts") to avoid mail delays. If you upload, postage is waived and we process faster. See policy: https://redwood.intra/benefits/foreign-claims (links internal).

People Ops: We can generate a temporary proof-of-coverage letter to email Farmacia Central. It will state active coverage dates and an emergency contact for verification (we’ll redact the policy number). ETA: within 24 hours — we’ll cc you and include contact details for verification.

Jordan: Thank you — please send it to farmacia@example.es and cc me (jordan.rivera@redwood.com). Uploading docs now.

People Ops: Got the upload (we see invoice_001.jpg). Next steps: please also upload the bank txn screenshot and a short English translation file. Once we have those we’ll route to claims and generate the coverage letter.

Jordan: Uploaded bank_txn.jpg and translation.txt. Anything else?

Claims Team: That should be enough to start. We may follow up if we need a provider attestation or translation clarification. Expect an internal claim number in ~48–72 hours. We’ll also confirm reimbursement currency conversion and estimated USD amount once processed.

People Ops: Coverage letter sent to farmacia@example.es and cc'd to you — message ID HR-176888-AUTO. Pharmacy confirmed receipt via auto-reply. If they ask for more, ping this thread and we’ll escalate. :thumbsup:

Jordan: :raised_hands: Really appreciate the quick help. I’ll follow up if pharmacy asks for anything else.

Zoe Patel: Glad that worked out — also saved a copy of the letter in my travel folder for next time.

Benefits Bot: Tip: keep digital copies of receipts in the portal — saves time next time you travel.
